name: Julius Lothar (von) Meyer
summary: German physical chemist known for his work on the periodic classification of elements and atomic weights.

summary: Physician and father of Julius Lothar Meyer.

name: Anna Sophie Wilhelmine Biermann
summary: Mother of Julius Lothar Meyer.

name: Oskar August Emil Meyer
summary: Brother of Julius Lothar Meyer and professor of physics in Breslau.

name: Dmitri Ivanovič Mendeleev
summary: Russian chemist known for formulating the Periodic Law and creating the periodic table.

name: Karl Seubert
summary: German chemist and colleague of Meyer who worked on atomic weights.

name: Robert Bunsen
summary: German chemist and professor at Heidelberg.

name: August Kekulé
summary: German organic chemist who presented type-theory to young chemists.

name: Franz Ernst Neumann
summary: German physicist and founder of theoretical physics as a university discipline in Germany.

name: Stanislao Cannizzaro
summary: Italian chemist who demanded recognition of Avogadro's theory at the Karlsruhe conference.

name: University of Zurich
summary: Swiss university where Meyer enrolled in 1851.

name: University of Würzburg
summary: German university where Meyer completed his Doctor of Medicine.

summary: German university where Meyer worked with Robert Bunsen.

name: University of Breslau

name: Forest Academy in Neustadt-Eberswalde
summary: Academy where Meyer held a position teaching mineralogy and chemistry.

summary: Institution where Meyer became professor of chemistry and director of the chemical laboratory.

summary: German university where Meyer received a full professorship and served as rector.

summary: British society of which Meyer became an honorary member.

summary: Town in Germany where Meyer was born.

name: Tübingen
summary: City in Germany where Meyer died and is buried.

summary: Textbook by Meyer on chemical theories and statics.
